item.observed: No working/not-working verdict is rendered even when the reader has a blocking error.
item.title: The operator still cannot tell whether the reader is working — Channel Reader only lists raw connection and activity fields without the required working or blocking-reason verdict

item.observed: Connected as the user is displayed alongside the stale 'No Telegram login saved' error.
item.title: After the operator logs in, the reader still reports that no Telegram login is saved — the new login error is never cleared on successful connection

item.observed: First status can return enabled=false, has_login=false and last_error=null for an enabled reader.
item.title: An enabled reader with no login can initially appear switched off instead of showing why it is disconnected — the status request does not wait for reader initialization

item.observed: A second failed resolution hits the repeat branch and clears the retry without sending.
item.title: A temporarily unreachable destination still permanently misses a deal — after the first channel succeeds, the repeat-only retry returns before checking the unresolved destination

item.observed: An unthreaded late reply newer than the current request is accepted for the current product.
item.title: Followers can still receive the wrong product after a slow Sankmo conversion — the new reply-to guard accepts late replies that have no reply-to field

item.observed: A response-body 'terminated' error is treated as retryable after the original send.
item.title: Followers can still receive a duplicate post after Telegram accepts a send but the response is lost — unrecognized transport or response-body errors release claims and retry the non-idempotent send

item.observed: After a restart last_read, last_sent, timing breakdown and last_error are null.
item.title: The operator loses the reader's last activity, error and newly added timing breakdown after a restart — status keeps them only in process memory

item.observed: Both destinations appear sent while total_ms and send_ms use the first destination's time.
item.title: The operator sees an incomplete total for posts to both channels — last_sent takes the first configured successful result even if the other channel confirmed later

item.observed: Last post sent says 'by bot' for every posting bot.
item.title: The operator cannot identify which bot sent the last reader post — status stores the generic word 'bot' rather than the selected bot name

item.observed: A direct conversion completed during link opening can be displayed as 0.00s.
item.title: The operator can mistake a slow direct-short-link conversion for an instant one — the converter timer starts only after its already-running conversion and short-link opening finish

item.observed: A slow repeat claim is included in convert_ms and service_ms even if conversion finished sooner.
item.title: The operator cannot measure converter speed independently from destination lookup and duplicate checks — the new timing records the parallel claim-and-conversion wall time as conversion time

item.observed: If all destination lookups fail, the reader retries without writing a Converter History row.
item.title: The operator cannot find failed channel-resolution attempts in Converter History — the reader throws before writing any history entry when every destination is unreachable

item.observed: Reader history contains a store and URLs but no product code or product title.
item.title: The operator cannot identify a logged product without opening its link — reader history saves neither the product code nor title and the history row renders neither

item.observed: A manual conversion suppresses the reader's empty message even if no reader posts exist.
item.title: The operator cannot tell that the reader has never posted when other conversions exist — Converter History only tests whether the entire mixed log is empty

item.observed: Reused conversions and full product URLs display numeric conversion/opening times, not a dash.
item.title: The operator is shown work as performed when a cached link skipped conversion or a full product URL needed no opening — reader timings always assign numbers and the display turns missing values into zero

item.observed: A conversion failure stores service_ms but its history row hides the converter duration.
item.title: The operator cannot see how long a failed reader conversion took — Converter History shows converter timing only for successful rows

item.observed: A send with unknown outcome is logged as failed with 'Post not sent'.
item.title: The operator is incorrectly told a timed-out deal was not posted even though Telegram may have delivered it — unknown send outcomes are logged as definitive failures

item.observed: Reader repeats enter the 'post to delete order' average; reader sends count as 'Telegram edit'.
item.title: The operator sees misleading reader speed and repeat summaries — history averages mix reader sends and skipped repeats with converter-bot edits and deletions

item.observed: PHONE_NUMBER_BANNED is shown as a temporary code block with 'Try again later'.
item.title: An operator with a banned Telegram account is told to retry later instead of being told the account is banned — the new login error mapper presents the ban as a temporary code restriction

item.observed: A source whose startup lookup fails is absent from sources[] used by every later poll.
item.title: Followers permanently miss deals from a source after a brief startup lookup failure — the reader marks the source failed but never retries adding it to the running poller

item.observed: A link converted in Convert Links creates no row in Converter History.
item.title: The operator cannot find or distinguish manual Convert Links activity in Converter History — the manual conversion endpoint never writes to the history collection

item.observed: A single destination post containing two product links generates two separate history rows.
item.title: The operator can mistake one multi-product reader post for multiple posts — history inserts and displays one row per link without a shared post identifier

item.title: The operator cannot tell at a glance whether the reader is working — Channel Reader only lists raw connection and activity fields without the required working or blocking-reason verdict
